streaming-callbacks-async.summary: Streaming cuts time to first token, not total latency, and a chain streams end to end only if every step after the model can transform a stream. Know the three ways to watch a run (stream/astream output chunks, astream_events for every component, agent stream modes), how callback handlers hook into it, and how the async methods behave when a component has no native async code.
points: Every Runnable has `invoke`, `batch`, `stream` and async twins `ainvoke`, `abatch`, `astream`, plus `batch_as_completed`/`abatch_as_completed` and `astream_events`. `astream` is an async generator: iterate it with `async for`, never `await` it.

`stream` yields the last step's output chunk by chunk: a chat model yields `AIMessageChunk`s, and `StrOutputParser` turns each into a string. A plain function (`RunnableLambda`) needs its whole input, so placed after the model it holds back the output until the end; placed before the model it costs nothing.

To keep streaming through custom code, pipe a generator function that takes an iterator of chunks; it is coerced to a `RunnableGenerator`. Wrapping the same generator in `RunnableLambda` first collects the whole input, then calls it.

`astream_events` defaults to `version="v2"` in langchain-core 1.x. Events are named `on_<type>_<start|stream|end>`: `on_chat_model_stream` carries `data["chunk"]`, parsers emit `on_parser_*`, tools and retrievers emit only start and end. Inner model tokens appear even when a later step blocks the final output.

Filter events with `include_names`, `include_types` (`chat_model`, `llm`, `parser`, `prompt`, `retriever`, `tool`, `chain`) and `include_tags`; include filters combine with OR, and `exclude_*` filters remove matches. Tags are inherited by child runs.

Chat models auto-stream: when a streaming-aware handler is attached (`astream_events`, LangGraph `messages` mode), `invoke` uses the streaming API internally and still returns one `AIMessage`. `disable_streaming=True` makes `stream` return a single chunk; `"tool_calling"` disables it only when tools are bound.

`create_agent` agents stream with `stream_mode`: `updates` gives per-step dicts keyed by node (`model`, `tools`), `messages` gives `(token, metadata)` tuples with `metadata["langgraph_node"]`, `custom` gives whatever tools send through `get_stream_writer()`, `values` gives full state. A list of modes yields `(mode, chunk)` tuples; `version="v2"` yields `StreamPart` dicts. The docs recommend `stream_events(version="v3")` for new apps.

Callback handlers subclass `BaseCallbackHandler` (or `AsyncCallbackHandler`) and override hooks such as `on_chat_model_start`, `on_llm_new_token(token, **kwargs)`, `on_llm_end`, `on_chain_*`, `on_tool_*`, `on_retriever_*` and `on_custom_event`. If `on_chat_model_start` is not implemented, chat models fall back to `on_llm_start` with stringified messages.

Handler errors are logged and swallowed unless the handler sets `raise_error = True`. In async runs, sync handlers run in a thread executor (unless `run_inline = True`) and async handlers are awaited on the loop. One handler instance serves concurrent runs, so key per-call state by `run_id`.

`dispatch_custom_event(name, data)` (or `adispatch_custom_event`) inside a Runnable or tool surfaces as `on_custom_event` in `astream_events` v2 and in handlers' `on_custom_event`; outside a run it raises `RuntimeError`.

Default async methods run the sync code in asyncio's thread pool, so a sync-only component still works under `await` without blocking the loop. `max_concurrency` in the config caps parallel calls for `batch`/`abatch`; `return_exceptions=True` returns failures in place; `abatch_as_completed` yields `(index, result)` out of order.

LangChain passes config through context variables. Before Python 3.11, asyncio tasks cannot carry a context, so in async code pass `config` explicitly to `ainvoke`/`astream`/`adispatch_custom_event`, and take a `writer` parameter instead of calling `get_stream_writer()`. In Jupyter use top-level `await`, not `asyncio.run`.
traps: Streaming does not reduce total generation time or token cost; it only shows the first tokens sooner.
A post-processing `RunnableLambda` at the end of a chain silently turns a token stream into one chunk at the end.
Calling sync `chain.invoke` or iterating `chain.stream` inside an `async def` FastAPI endpoint blocks the event loop and prevents cancellation on disconnect; use `ainvoke`/`astream`.
SSE frames end at a blank line, so a raw newline in a token breaks the frame; JSON-encode payloads. Clients must buffer across network chunks, because one chunk can hold part of a frame.
A tool that calls `get_stream_writer()` fails when invoked directly outside a LangGraph run, which breaks naive unit tests.
Naming the token parameter anything other than `token` in a sync `on_llm_new_token` makes every call fail, and the error is only logged.
Storing per-call state such as a start time on `self` in a handler gives wrong numbers under `abatch` or concurrent requests.
